A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same PAS research work. All supplied pages support comparison, including v1's three-page theoretical supplement, which is absent from v2; this is an observable omission rather than an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original nine-benchmark comparisons in Table 2, offset and sampling-rate experiments in Figures 4–5, and inference-throughput measurements in Section 3.4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results in Table 1, experiments in Figures 4–5, and throughput measurements in Section 3.4.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 3.4 retain the same training-free procedure: apply temporal offsets only to video-token queries after positional encoding, then use normal attention and head aggregation. No component or inference step changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same four action-recognition datasets and five general video benchmarks. Nyquist-valid sampling and the sub-Nyquist Breakfast scenario remain unchanged; the dataset overview is merely renumbered from Table 1 to Table 2.

E2.justification: The corresponding results tables contain the same six strategies: the Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct backbone, SlowFast-LLaVA, TS-LLaVA, PAS, and the two PAS-stacked variants. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The backbone, metrics, matched token budgets, decoding and preprocessing controls remain unchanged. Both use two phase groups with offsets [0, 0.5], the same offset sweep, and the same sampling-ratio evaluation design.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 and Figures 4–5 retain the same offset-sensitivity and sampling-rate analyses on the same four datasets. Figure 1's illustrative failure also remains. The omitted supplement contains theoretical derivations rather than additional empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Empirical uncertainty reporting is unchanged: both retain the throughput measurements with identical ± values and the same statistical-indistinguishability statements. No run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All 78 scores match between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 1. Figures 4–5 and throughput results also remain unchanged; for example, PAS retains 18.3 Jester accuracy, 48.2 Kinetics-700 accuracy, and throughput of (76.8 ± 4.0) × 10^3 tokens/s.

T1.justification: The main-text Theorems 1–4 and Equations 1–10 remain, but v2 omits v1's entire supplement. This removes explicit assumptions A1–A4, concentration and finite-m approximation bounds, the exact spectral Lipschitz derivation, and proofs concerning smoothing and spectrum preservation (Equations 11–35). V2 still refers to these supplementary materials.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: temporal RoPE causes phase sensitivity, PAS smooths modulation without training, spectral magnitudes are preserved under Nyquist conditions, and matched-token performance improves with negligible overhead.

C2.justification: Omitting the supplement removes its specific explanation of energy redistribution among overlapping aliases and its interpretation of sensitivity through the first spectral moment. The main-text explanations of smoothing, finite-window limitations, Nyquist requirements, and diminishing gains under denser sampling remain.

D1.justification: The implementation hook, video masking, MHA/GQA broadcasting, bin/frame unit guidance, default offsets, complexity discussion, and NVIDIA A100 80 GB hardware disclosure are retained. The code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 28 works are cited, and PAS retains the same positioning relative to video architectures, positional encodings, and training-free baselines. Section 2 condenses descriptions of earlier architectures without changing the paper's substantive relationship to them.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized copyedits, shortens the opening related-work paragraph and conclusion, updates affiliations and contact information, and adds acknowledgements. The main section sequence and narrative remain stable; the supplementary proof section is omitted.

P2.justification: The results and dataset tables exchange numbering and placement. Figure 3 moves beneath Algorithm 1 and corrects its final offset label from h_n to t_n. Figures 4–5 move upward on the page; their plots and the other figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The supplied v2 loses the detailed assumptions, bounds, and derivations supporting the paper's central theoretical contribution, while retaining the theorem claims and references to absent supplementary proofs. This substantially reduces completeness and readers' ability to assess those guarantees. Limited editorial and layout improvements do not compensate, and the empirical evidence is unchanged.
